title: Fast-path router: prefill probe, candidate scoring heuristics, and graceful rollback for two-stage decoding
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement a lightweight fast-path router that probes prefill signals to pick a candidate model for speculative decode, scores acceptance probability, and provides deterministic graceful fallback when the acceptance check fails. This ticket covers algorithm spec, kernel/attention considerations that affect latencies, required instrumentation, and a deployment plan with rollback controls.
acceptance_criteria: Router can pick a preferred fast-path candidate with O(1) probe overhead per request (no more than 0.4 ms added median latency on p50 for standard 512-token prefill workloads)
Acceptance heuristic implemented so that false acceptance rate <= 1% on sampled evaluation prompts compared to baseline full-decode quality metrics
Fallback path triggers automatically and recovers within the request lifecycle (no dropped responses); end-to-end tail latency degradation on fallback bounded to SLA targets
Telemetry emitted: candidate_score, acceptance_decision, kv_cache_hit, kernel_variant_used, route_latency_ms, fallback_reason, acceptance_threshold_version
Feature flag + canary rollout exists and can be reverted instantly via console toggle; rollout health checks defined
implementation_notes:
Core pieces:
- Probe strategy: use a single-prefix fast prefill probe that evaluates short context prefixes and lightweight model scorer (smaller quantized candidate) to predict acceptance. Avoid full KV prefill to keep probe cheap.
- Candidate scoring: logistic score combining model logit-consistency metric, perplexity delta on prefix, and hardware fingerprint score (kernel suitability). Tune weights per deployment tier.
- Kernel selection impact: ensure probe uses same kernel path or a known compatible fallback kernel mapping to avoid misaligned latency/accuracy assumptions. Add kernel_fingerprint to telemetry.
- Attention optimization: for probe path, use reduced attention window and optimized causal mask to reduce compute; ensure decode scheduler supports mixed-sequence-length batching so probe and main decode can share queues.
- Prefill/decode scheduling: implement a two-stage scheduling token pipeline where probe prefills in a low-priority prefetch lane and main decode can preempt if probe indicates low acceptance probability.
- KV cache handling: when probe indicates acceptance, ensure efficient KV promotion to the main decode execution to avoid duplicate work; implement shallow copy semantics and reference counting to prevent double allocation.
- Fallback: deterministic rollback path that cancels probe result and routes request to baseline model variant (or full prefill+decode) with preserved tokens. Ensure idempotency and no partial stream emission.
- Safety: acceptance thresholds versioned and tied to an eval harness; put guard rails so thresholds cannot be raised without approval.
- Observability: add per-request sampling and aggregated histograms for acceptance_rate by model, kernel_variant, region, and customer tier.
- Tests: synthetic eval corpus, shadowing runs against production traffic (1% initially), and notebook to visualize threshold trade-offs.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Unit + integration tests in CI and local perf bench (<2 weeks). Phase 1: Shadow mode (no production routing) collecting telemetry for 2 weeks. Phase 2: Canary enable at 1% traffic with strict SLO monitors for latency and quality; hold 3 days. Phase 3: Ramp 5% -> 25% -> 75% with automated rollback criteria. Phase 4: Full enable and postmortem review. Each phase gated by a console toggle and feature flag; emergency kill-switch will immediately route all requests to baseline. Define metric gates: acceptance_rate within expected band, false_accept_rate <1%, p99 latency not degraded >20%.
